title: Real-time schema rotator and lightweight transform layer for console metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: frequent lightweight changes to console telemetry event shapes (field renames, optional deprecations, simple derived attributes) force consumers and pipelines to roll code or run heavyweight ETL jobs, causing small but recurring incidents and increased operational load. Proposal: introduce a low-latency "schema rotator" service in the ingest path that performs safe on-the-fly transformations and compatibility checks using sandboxed WASM adapters and a compact schema registry. The rotator should be able to: 1) route events by tenant and schema version, 2) apply deterministic, idempotent transforms (rename, type-cast, field flatten/expand, simple arithmetic derives), 3) surface schema drift alerts and automated compat checks, 4) fall back to a safe passthrough and dead-letter for unknown/unfixable events. This avoids full pipeline restarts while keeping downstream stores schema-stable.
goals: Add a low-latency transform layer that increases end-to-end P99 latency by <2% for typical console ingest traffic
Support concurrent coexisting schema versions per-tenant (min: 3 versions) with deterministic routing
Enable on-the-fly safe renames and simple derives via sandboxed WASM plugins
Provide drift detection and alerting integrated with Console (dashboard + SLAs)
Reduce weekly manual ETL jobs related to schema fixes by 80% within first month of roll-out
acceptance_criteria: Integration test harness demonstrating schema rotation with 3 active versions and zero restarts
Benchmark: median additional CPU <5% and P99 latency impact <2% on representative staging workload
End-to-end contract test that ensures transformed events match downstream parquet/OLAP schema
Operational runbook and observed dashboard with SLOs for error-rate and transformation latency
Canary rollout plan and automatic rollback on >0.5% increase in error-rate for a single tenant
tasks: Design doc: describe rotator architecture, routing rules, schema registry model (Confluence link in links)
Prototype WASM adapter harness and safe API for transforms
Implement rotator ingress hook (Kafka/ingest-proxy) with per-tenant routing and cache
Add compatibility check service and automated drift detector (daily and realtime modes)
Create test harness with synthetic event generator and downstream simulator
Build dashboards: transform latency, per-tenant error-rate, schema version distribution
Canary rollout to 5 internal tenants, iterate on transform language ergonomics
Document runbook and add alerts to PagerDuty on repeat transform failures
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with infra and product. Agreed success metrics and canary cadence.
2026-02-26: Prototype WASM adapter API v0.1 completed. Basic rename + type-cast transforms working in local harness.
2026-03-03: Ingest-proxy hook implemented as feature flag; end-to-end baseline tests show ~1.1% latency overhead on median requests.
2026-03-09: Compatibility checker PoC detects subtle float->string drift for historical batch backfills; added automatic DLQ routing for unfixable payloads.
2026-03-12: Security review request submitted for WASM sandboxing model; awaiting SecOps feedback (ticket SEC-4821).
notes: Design trade-offs: chose WASM for transform sandboxing to enable safe tenant-provided logic without restarting services.
Alternative considered: schema-on-write with full ETL; rejected due to operational overhead and slower iteration for product teams.
Potential follow-ups: add a UI in Console for quick field-mapping proposals and previewing transformed events per-tenant.
